note: Eighth core term is LLM — Mohammad listed seven named cores; CoS allowed +1 for a clean set of eight. Curriculum: use these defs only; do not invent.

entries.plain_def: A large AI model trained on huge amounts of text so it can understand and generate language — predicting the next token, over and over, until it writes a full answer.
entries.milestone_note: Transformer architecture paper (“Attention Is All You Need”) unlocked modern LLMs; consumer chatbots followed later (e.g. ChatGPT Nov 2022).
entries.source_title: What Are Large Language Models (LLMs)? — IBM

entries.plain_def: The small chunks an AI model actually reads and writes — often pieces of words, not whole words. Models bill and limit context by token count, not by character count.
entries.milestone_note: Subword BPE for NMT popularized in 2015–2016; per-token API pricing became the industry norm with commercial LLM APIs from ~2020.
entries.source_title: What Is a Token in AI? An Explainer — Couchbase

entries.plain_def: A defined way for one program to talk to another — a contract of requests and responses — so apps can share data and features without sharing their internal code.
entries.milestone_note: General computing concept (decades old). In AI products, “the API” usually means the HTTP endpoints you call to send prompts and get model output.

entries.plain_def: An AI system where the model itself decides what to do next — picking tools, looping on a goal — instead of only answering inside a fixed, pre-written script.
entries.milestone_note: Agent/tool-use patterns exploded in product use through 2024–2026; definitions still vary by vendor. LangChain’s production framing: the LLM owns application control flow.
entries.source_title: What is an AI agent? — LangChain

entries.plain_def: An open standard for plugging AI assistants into tools and data sources through one shared protocol — like a USB-C port for AI apps — instead of a custom connector for every pair.
entries.milestone_note: Open-sourced by Anthropic on Nov 25, 2024. Spec and docs: modelcontextprotocol.io.
entries.source_title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol — Anthropic

entries.plain_def: A fair-code workflow automation tool where you connect apps and AI steps on a visual canvas (or with code). Self-host for free, or use their cloud. Name = “nodemation,” said “n-eight-n.”
entries.milestone_note: Public launch October 2019 (Berlin); founded by Jan Oberhauser. Company n8n GmbH registered Nov 2019.

entries.plain_def: Anthropic’s family of AI assistants and models — chat + API — trained to be helpful, honest, and harmless. You use it in the Claude apps or call it from your own software.
entries.milestone_note: Anthropic introduced Claude publicly on Mar 14, 2023. Model lineup has since expanded (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus / later generations).

entries.plain_def: xAI’s conversational AI assistant — chat, search, voice, and creation tools — built to answer with real-time context and a less-filtered style than many rivals.
entries.milestone_note: xAI announced Grok on Nov 3–4, 2023 (early beta / waitlist). Later available via X Premium tiers, grok.com, and mobile apps.
